name: Hashed collection misuse: equals overridden without consistent hashCode
description: A class overrides equals(Object) (value-based equality) but does not define a matching hashCode() implementation. Java then uses Object.hashCode (identity-based), violating the equals/hashCode contract. When such objects are used in hashed collections (HashMap/HashSet), logically equal instances may reside in different buckets, causing contains/get/remove failures and enabling duplicate logical keys. This frequently manifests as protocol/state bugs: cache duplication, inconsistent deduplication, or message/state comparisons failing after re-materialization.

trigger_conditions.test_shape: Tests that rely on hashed collections for deduplication or lookup, especially across object reconstruction (parsing/deserialization/copy).
trigger_conditions.input_properties: Two distinct instances have equal value fields and equals returns true; one instance is used to store, another is used to look up.

example.description: A protocol deduplication layer uses a value-like key (source, streamId, seq) in a HashSet/HashMap to detect replays and to cache decoded frames. The key overrides equals(Object) but forgets to override hashCode(). After re-parsing the same logical frame, a new key instance compares equal but hashes by identity, so contains/get fail and the system accepts duplicates or misses cached entries, leading to inconsistent state and failing assertions.
